t: Rutland House is a name that belonged to at least three London houses occupied by the Earls and Dukes of Rutland. One was on Aldersgate Street, where the playwright Sir William Davenant converted a room into a private theatre in the 1650s. Another stood in Knightsbridge, on a six-acre site, until it was demolished in the 1830s. The third is on Park Place in St James's. Prince Frederick, Duke of York and Albany, the second son of George the Third, died at a Rutland House in 1827. Had he lived three more years, he would have become king.
